objects.description: short-lived daemon-authenticated inspection used to create or refresh a code worktree
mutable Project pointer selecting its default code execution context
immutable expected Git snapshot stored with an executable task

entries.evidence: Design: local daemon owns Git facts; server stores only daemon-authenticated result.
Design registration flow names desktop/CLI request, daemon completion, API persistence, and UI confirmation.
Design defines pending, completed, consumed, and expired lifecycle.
Expiry and daemon reachability leave existing binding visible; user starts a new inspection.
One-time consume and optimistic refresh updated_at check are specified.
Inspection is an ephemeral proof and does not publish a readable version.
Completion is daemon-authenticated and bound to requesting user, workspace, daemon, and expiry.
Inspection and result IDs, typed errors, and inspected state are exposed in the contract.
Re-reviewed against current daemon local-path safety boundary and handler daemon credential boundary.
Project owns nullable default pointer; code_worktree owns the verified checkout record.
Project bind/unbind API writes pointer; enqueue resolves it; desktop displays it; web is read-only.
Nullable pointer, bind/unbind, and deletion guard are specified.
Incompatible local_directory and dirty state reject assignment with typed errors.
Bind locks worktree and delete checks pointers transactionally.
Bind affects only future tasks; unbind is explicit and leaves old task snapshots readable.
Workspace ownership and same-daemon runtime validation are required.
Project UI shows binding facts; project binding emits project:updated and initiating worktree mutations invalidate the local query.
Design preserves the existing project_resource model as separate compatibility surface.
Revision names agent_task_queue.worktree_context as the immutable stored snapshot.
Enqueue writes snapshot; claim returns it; daemon preflight consumes it; retry/rerun rules are explicit.
Non-worktree tasks use {}; active snapshots protect deletion; terminal task history remains auditable.
Preflight drift fails before launch; retry inherits snapshot; rerun resolves a new binding.
Task creation and retry take KEY SHARE on the referenced worktree; deletion takes the conflicting worktree lock, then checks non-terminal snapshots.
A Project change affects future tasks only; queued snapshots are not rewritten.
Server rejects runtime/daemon mismatch before inserting task; daemon rechecks local Git before execution.
Task logs and payload include worktree ID, path, expected and observed Git state.
Revision aligns server claim-time project loading with an explicit stored task context requirement.
